extra.message: User-controlled input from request.GET.get('expr') is passed directly to eval(). Although __builtins__ is cleared, eval() on attacker-controlled input is a code-injection sink and can be escaped (e.g. via class/attribute traversal) to achieve remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: User input from request.GET.get('fragment') is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string that is then rendered and returned as text/html. This is a server-side template injection allowing arbitrary code execution (e.g. {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}).

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: A JSON body parsed from the request (payload.get('filter', payload)) is passed directly as the query filter to MongoClient().ops.records.find_one(query). An attacker can inject MongoDB operators such as {"$where": "..."} or {"field": {"$ne": null}} to bypass filters or execute JavaScript, enabling NoSQL injection.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: User-controlled name from request.GET.get('name') is joined to BASE_EXPORT_DIR with Path(/) and written via target.write_bytes(request.body). A value like '../../../etc/cron.d/evil' escapes the export directory, allowing arbitrary file write anywhere the process can write.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: User input from request.GET.get('copyline') is concatenated directly into an HTML string which is returned with content_type='text/html' via HttpResponse. The value is not HTML-escaped, enabling reflected cross-site scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The 'lane' value is read from request.GET/request.POST and passed directly to redirect(lane) without validating that it is an internal URL. An attacker can supply an absolute URL (e.g. https://evil.com) to redirect users off-site (open redirect).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: logger.warning() writes the request body and the Authorization header (request.headers.get('authorization'), i.e. bearer credentials) to the application log. Logging bearer tokens exposes credentials in log files that may be accessed by unauthorized parties.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Unlike every other ops endpoint, patient_identity_ping_345 does not call _wrk_gate() (the x-internal-token check) and has no @login_required. It is therefore accessible by unauthenticated users, exposing an internal operations endpoint without any authentication.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Hardcoded verifier credentials are embedded in source: known = {'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'} and used to authorize access. Anyone with source access knows these secrets, defeating the verification check.

The response reflects the request Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows any arbitrary cross-origin site to make credentialed requests and read the responses, enabling cross-origin data theft.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection: '0' and empties Content-Security-Policy, disabling browser XSS filtering and content security policy protections for the response.

Elevated access ('lane': 'elevated', 'payroll': 'full') is granted based on a client-controlled value: request.COOKIES.get('ops_badge') or the x-ops-badge header. A user can simply set this cookie/header to 'lead' to obtain elevated privileges, which is improper authorization.

cwe: CWE-602: Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security

extra.message: length is taken from request.GET.get('length') as an int and used to drive range(length) in a ''.join(...) call. There is no upper bound, so a request with length=1000000000 forces allocation of a multi-GB string, causing denial of service. Additionally the random module (not secrets) is used to generate the code.

cwe: CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

extra.message: ssl._create_unverified_context() is used to disable certificate verification for the outbound urllib.request.urlopen() call. This makes the connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks because the server certificate is not validated.

The endpoint returns sensitive values in the JSON response: a partner sync API key ('sync_key': 'tok_live_partner_sync') and a tax identifier/SSN-formatted value ('tax_ref': '739-44-1982'). Exposing API keys and tax/SSN-like identifiers in an endpoint response is sensitive data exposure.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: prescription_edit only checks 'if request.user.is_clinician and rx.provider != ...'. It never verifies the user is a clinician or clinic_admin (unlike prescription_create which does). Patients and front_desk users pass the check and can POST to edit any prescription, including the medication_name, dosage, instructions, quantity and even the patient field via PrescriptionForm. This is a broken access control / missing authorization flaw.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: user_toggle_active performs a state-changing operation (user.is_active = not user.is_active; user.save()) but never checks request.method == 'POST'. The URL therefore works over GET, which is exempt from Django's CSRF protection. A malicious page can embed e.g. to CSRF an admin into enabling/disabling arbitrary user accounts.

SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded insecure default 'django-insecure-local-dev-only-change-in-production' when the environment variable is not set. If deployed without SECRET_KEY set, the known key allows session cookie forgery and CSRF token bypass.

DEBUG defaults to True when the DEBUG environment variable is not set. Running with DEBUG=True in production exposes detailed stack traces, settings, and source code, and also disables SECURE_* cookie flags (SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE/CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE are 'not DEBUG').

The database PASSWORD falls back to a hardcoded default 'clinic_pass' when DB_PASSWORD is not set. Hardcoded default database credentials can be used to access the database if the environment variable is not configured.

Seed data creates accounts with hardcoded weak passwords ('adminpass', 'clinicianpass', 'frontdeskpass', 'patientpass') and additional users use the shared password 'clinicianpass'/'patientpass'. If this seed command is run in a non-local environment these weak default credentials allow trivial account takeover.
